anchors.shared_content: Every completion of a partial labeling must avoid small circuits.
anchors.novelty_delta: Generator-induced labels plus batched lookup give a near-threshold two-polarity formula footprint bound.
anchors.claim_reset: Do not claim a new meta-complexity problem without a direct Partial MCSP comparison.

anchors.shared_content: A small hardwired exception set gives a cheap completion circuit.
anchors.novelty_delta: The dictionary is shared across the whole generated batch, reducing naive M K ell comparison to near-linear batch-plus-dictionary size.
anchors.claim_reset: Present as the main technical contribution.

anchors.shared_content: A small labeled set may rule out a hypothesis class.
anchors.novelty_delta: The paper requires all completions of a generator-induced source function to remain above the circuit threshold.
anchors.claim_reset: Frame as structured refuter certificate complexity, not a general test-suite theory.

anchors.shared_content: A certificate fixes coordinates that force membership in a concept or property class.
anchors.novelty_delta: The paper adds row, polarity, and quotient geometry for an induced-hardness property.
anchors.claim_reset: Use certificate-complexity language and avoid new proof-complexity measure claims.

anchors.shared_content: Unforced rows can be completed to a near-constant source function.
anchors.novelty_delta: The theorem separates row count from the forcing numbers of the aggregator.
anchors.claim_reset: Keep as a supporting lemma unless matched by examples or proof-system extraction.

anchors.shared_content: Equality links restrict completions to an affine subspace before sparse patching.
anchors.novelty_delta: The quotient theorem states residual distance from constants after sound equality identifications.
anchors.claim_reset: State that nonlinear SAT semantics and self-reduction are outside scope.

anchors.shared_content: A semantic proof may impose local Boolean relations between formula labels.
anchors.novelty_delta: The semantic-relation support theorem shows that a support-local audit must contain a standard relation-membership certificate for each imposed relation instance; for y=y0 OR y1, unsat branches require parent and both children. The acyclic OR-tree theorem gives the eliminated-frontier certificate for bounded OR self-reduction trees, and the OR-DAG theorem shows that sharing and repeated reachable frontier formulas do not change the cost after sound quotienting.
anchors.claim_reset: Do not claim a full residual-completion theorem for hidden, learned-clause, cyclic, or arbitrary SAT self-reduction closures.

anchors.shared_content: A finite exposed semantic frontier, adaptive decision tree, or adaptive branching program has ordinary Boolean certificate complexity.
anchors.novelty_delta: The acyclic Boolean frontier theorem identifies support-locality with root plus pointwise certificate complexity for the induced frontier function, the visible-adaptive theorems add that logged transcript-path or computation-path support is sufficient only because the whole adaptive control object is checker-visible, and the hidden-transcript separator shows that an uncertified transcript summary alone can mask all-frontier OR support.
anchors.claim_reset: Do not claim hidden adaptive SAT self-reduction closure without a checker-visible frontier circuit or adaptive control object, quotienting, and support budget.

anchors.shared_content: A source lower bound for a polylog-query SAT carrier could transfer to SAT lower bounds.
anchors.novelty_delta: The paper factors local certificate costs conditional on the source lower bound.
anchors.claim_reset: Demote to calibration unless an explicit hard source theorem is added.

anchors.shared_content: A proof may replace a local object by a representative after proving same-theory equivalence.
anchors.novelty_delta: The Qrep proposition makes the temporal support condition explicit: quotient compression is transparent only when the same-theory certificate forest is displayed and charged before first representative use.
anchors.claim_reset: Do not count delayed quotient certificates, representative rebinding, or advice-chosen representatives as transparent support.

anchors.shared_content: Strong proof systems can encode semantic information nonlocally.

anchors.shared_content: Constructive, large, useful properties enter the natural-proofs regime.
anchors.novelty_delta: Sparse local certificates may avoid largeness.

novelty_delta_accounting.before_after_understanding_shift: completion-sound evidence that a generated labeling is hard must either expose a large local footprint, or supply an auditable proof-system mechanism that computes the same footprint from the proof artifact

claim_boundary: The batched formula-footprint theorem is the main technical novelty.
Row forcing and quotient distance are supporting structural lemmas.
The SAT section is conditional calibration.
Proof-complexity claims require a separate extraction theorem.

Exposed acyclic semantic frontiers and checker-visible adaptive decision-tree or branching-program frontiers reduce to ordinary Boolean certificate complexity, but hidden adaptive SAT semantics still require a separate support theorem; transcript summaries alone are separated from sound support audits.
The draft is not a new general hardness-magnification theorem.
